Preparation of TBDPS-EVR under Unoptimized Conditions
A solution of triflate 1b (2.60 g, 6.01 mmol, 2 equiv) in toluene (12 mL) was added to a suspension of RAP (2.74 g, 3.00 mmol) in toluene (10 mL) followed by DIPEA (0.81 g, 6.27 mmol, 2.1 equiv). The reaction vessel was sealed with a septum, and the reaction mixture was stirred at 50  C. After 5 and 21 h, triflate 1b (2.60 g, 6.01 mmol, 2 equiv each time) and EDIPA (0.81 g, 6.27 mmol, 2.1 equiv each time) were added till full consumption of RAP (monitored by TLC, 6 equiv of 1b and 6.3 equiv of DIPEA in total). After 26 h, pyridine (1.42 g, 6 equiv) in hexane (150 mL) was added, and the reaction mixture was stirred for 30 min at room temperature. The formed precipitate was filtered off and washed with hexane/ethyl acetate = 3:1 (2   20 mL). The filtrate was consequentially washed with 5%aq citric acid (2   25 mL), saturated NaHCO3 (25 mL), and brine (2   12 mL). After that, it was dried over Na2SO4 (5 g), filtered, and concentrated under reduced pressure at 35  C. Crude reaction mass (5.05 g) was obtained after drying at 10 2 mbar for 2 h. TBDPS-EVR with a purity of more than 95% was obtained by silica gel (150 g) flash chromatography with DCM and ethyl acetate in 48% (1.73 g) yield.

Preparation of TBDPS-EVR under Optimized Alkylation Conditions and No Hydrolysis
A solution of triflate 1b (6.05 g, 14.00 mmol, 2.5 equiv) and PMP (2.64 g, 17.00 mmol, 3 equiv) in acetonitrile (4 mL) was added to a suspension of RAP (5.10 g, 5.58 mmol) in acetonitrile (2 mL). The reaction vessel was sealed with a septum, and the reaction mixture was stirred for 44 h at 22 25  C. Pyridine (2.2 g) was added, and the reaction mixture was stirred for 30 min at room temperature, concentrated under reduced pressure at 35  C, and dried at 10 2 mbar for 2 h. Methyl tert-butyl ether (MTBE) (50 mL) was added to the residue at 35  C. The formed precipitate was filtered off and washed with MTBE (2   20 mL). The filtrate was washed with 5%aq citric acid (2   25 mL), saturated NaHCO3 (25 mL), and brine (2   12 mL). Extracts were dried over Na2SO4 (5 g), filtered and concentrated under reduced pressure at 35  C, and dried at 10 2 mbar for 2 h, affording 9.9 g of crude reaction mass. The residue was purified by silica gel (150 g) flash chromatography with DCM and ethyl acetate eluting system, affording TBDPS-EVR with a purity of more than 95% in 50% (3.37 g) yield.

Preparation of TBDPS-EVR with Developed Technology
A solution of triflate 1b (123.2 g, 0.28 mol, 2.5 equiv) and PMP (53.1 g, 0.34 mol, 3 equiv) in acetonitrile (50 mL) was added to a suspension of RAP (104.5 g, 0.11 mol) in acetonitrile (55 mL). The reaction vessel was sealed with a septum, and the reaction mixture was stirred for 43 h at 30 C. Methanol (1.12 L) was added, and the reaction mixture was cooled to 2-5 C. A 0.3 M solution of HCl in MeOH was added to pH 1.9, and the reaction mixture was stirred at this pH for 1.5 h at 2-5 C. A solution of 5% NaHCO3 (35 mL) was added to adjust the pH to 6.5-7, and the reaction mixture was diluted with water (650 mL) and extracted with a mixture of hexane/ethyl acetate = 1:1 (1700 mL, 2   600 mL). Extracts were dried over Na2SO4, filtered and concentrated under reduced pressure at 35 C, and dried at 10-2 mbar for 2 h, affording 158.1 g of crude reaction mass. The residue was purified by silica gel (3   950 g) flash chromatography in hexane and propan-2-ol (gradient from 2 to 5% of propan-2-ol), affording TBDPS-EVR with a purity of more than 95% in 59% (80.3 g) yield.

PdCl 2 (dppf) (1 mol%), B 2 (pin) 2 ,KOAc, and MeTHF at 80  C proved to be the optimal reactionconditions and delivered a high yield (85-90%) of the arylboro-nate ester 12 and arylboronic acid 10 as a 1:1 mixture after10-15 h (Scheme 3).13 Upon reaction workup, pinacol exchangefrom boron resulted in a  uctuating boronate ester-boronicacid ratio with each workup step. 14 To circumvent the pinacolexchange, treatment of the arylboronate ester and arylboronicacid mixture in MeTHF with sodium periodate (NaIO 4 ) in-duced an oxidative cleavage of the free pinacol 13 in solution.15 Theconversion of pinacol 13 to 2 equiv of acetone eliminated thepotential to regenerate the boronate ester 12 and drove theequilibrium to the arylboronic acid 10.
